title: RCACard
description: Final synthesized RCA card produced from structured reasoning artifacts, evidence retrieval, and constrained LLM synthesis.

generated_at.description: Timestamp when the RCA card was generated.

input_artifacts.description: References to key input artifacts used during synthesis.

executive_summary.description: Analyst-facing summary of the current RCA conclusion and review posture.

conclusion_type.description: Epistemic standing of the RCA conclusion. hypothesis_supported: primary candidate is A-series with non-trivial evidence posture. hypothesis_speculative: primary is B-series or all candidates have zero telemetry signal. no_adequate_hypothesis: no candidate met minimum requirements or all evidence is absent — treat the card as a review placeholder, not a conclusion.

depth_incomplete_reason.description: Present when depth_complete=false. Explains which depth layer is unresolved and what data or causal evidence would complete it.

causal_depth_level.description: Which causal depth layer this monitoring item addresses.

success_criteria.description: Measurable criterion that closes this monitoring item when met.

hypothesis_type.description: Hypothesis type copied or derived from the selected causality candidate.

narrative.description: Human-readable explanation of the selected primary hypothesis.

why_primary.description: Explicit reasons this hypothesis is ranked above alternatives.

uncertainties.description: Known uncertainties, unresolved contradictions, or missing evidence relevant to the primary hypothesis.

composite_score.description: Non-probabilistic ORDINAL RANKING score: a weighted blend of heuristic structural/temporal/telemetry/evidence/governance sub-scores. It is NOT a calibrated probability — 0.72 does not mean '72% likely'. Use it only to rank hypotheses relative to one another; interpret likelihood via confidence_label. See card-level score_interpretation.

alternatives.description: Alternative non-primary hypotheses considered during synthesis.

composite_score.description: Non-probabilistic ordinal ranking score (weighted heuristic blend), not a calibrated probability. See card-level score_interpretation.

supports.description: Short statements describing what supports this alternative.

weaknesses.description: Short statements describing what weakens this alternative.

contributing_causes.description: Contributing mechanisms that are causally relevant but not selected as the primary hypothesis.

evidence.description: Evidence records included in the RCA card for traceability.

support_role.description: How this evidence is being used in the RCA card.

linked_candidate_id.description: Candidate hypothesis this evidence most directly relates to, if applicable.

recommended_actions.description: Recommended next actions tied to the RCA output.

target_causal_depth.description: Which causal-depth layer this action primarily addresses.

expected_observation_if_true.description: What observation or result would strengthen the linked hypothesis if this action is taken.

analyst_review.description: Explicit analyst review gates and unresolved decision items.

ccf_summary.description: Common-cause failure summary block. Emitted when ≥2 candidates form a plausible common-cause cluster (suspected_ccf=true) or when any common-cause signal is present. Absence of this block means no common-cause signal was detected.

suspected_ccf.description: True when ≥2 candidates with medium/high CCF confidence share a plausible common mechanism and the top CCF score ≥ 0.45.

ccf_confidence.description: Confidence derived from the highest common-cause score among clustered candidates.

shared_mechanism_ids.description: KG node IDs of shared dependency or upstream components driving the CCF signal.

affected_trains.description: Train IDs that are out-of-service and linked to clustered CCF candidates, if known.

affected_candidate_ids.description: Candidate IDs that form the common-cause cluster.

rationale.description: Analyst-facing narrative summarising the CCF signal and recommended scope of investigation.

human_performance_assessment.description: Step 6 human and organizational performance assessment (v32 A–L taxonomy). Populated when a G (human performance), I (change control), or L (organisational/systemic) category candidate is retained. Design (H), surveillance/testing (J) and vendor/procurement (K) are NOT human-performance findings and are excluded from this block.

applicable.description: True when at least one G/I/L candidate is retained in the card.

category_flags.description: Which human/organisational causal categories (G, I, L) are present among retained candidates.

L.description: Organisational / systemic — training, safety culture, resource, corrective-action programme

findings.description: One structured finding per retained G/I/L candidate.

performance_mode.description: Human/organisational performance mode inferred from the v32 category (G→execution_error, I→change_management_gap, L→organisational_gap). Legacy values retained for backward compatibility.

corrective_action_ids.description: IDs of recommended_actions[] that address this finding.

regulatory_reference.description: Optional AP-913 / 10 CFR reference relevant to this human performance category.

provenance_note.description: Explanation when applicable=false or when human-performance data is limited.

prevention_analysis.description: Defense-in-depth 'why was it not prevented?' assessment for the primary hypothesis (metamodel §: 'which barriers failed, which held, and why'). Deterministically derived from PM/surveillance compliance, condition-monitoring detection, and the primary candidate's barrier-logic gate — distinct from the structural safety-function impact map in barrier_analysis. Absent for a NONE primary.

applicable.description: True when at least one defense-in-depth barrier could be assessed (held or gap) for the primary cause.

barriers.description: One row per assessed defense-in-depth layer.

barrier_type.description: Defense-in-depth layer: preventive maintenance / surveillance, condition monitoring / detection, or protection-logic / safety-function barrier.

status.description: held = barrier functioned; gap = barrier absent/failed/degraded and did not prevent the failure; not_evaluated = insufficient data; not_applicable = layer not relevant to this cause.

basis.description: Deterministic basis for the status (e.g. failed PM check ids, detection precursors, barrier-logic gate outcome).

detail.description: Optional supporting detail (check names, sensor ids, safety-function names).

failed_or_missing_barriers.description: barrier_type values whose status is 'gap' — the layers that did not prevent the failure.

why_not_prevented.description: Analyst-facing narrative answering 'why was it not prevented?' by naming the barrier gaps, or explaining the data limitation when none could be assessed.

provenance_note.description: Explanation of inputs used and any data limitations.

score_interpretation.description: N-4 transparency block: states how composite_score and its interval are to be read, so the number is never mistaken for a calibrated probability.

score_type.description: composite_score is an ordinal ranking score, not a probability or frequency.

is_probability.description: Always false — composite_score does not express a probability or likelihood percentage.

is_calibrated.description: Always false — weights and relation priors are hand-set and not calibrated against outcome frequencies.

interval_meaning.description: What any score confidence interval encodes (data availability / degradation), NOT statistical/sampling uncertainty.

note.description: Analyst-facing guidance on how to read the score and which field (confidence_label) to use for likelihood.

gate_disposition.description: F-4 elimination-first audit: makes explicit that hard gates are dispositive — a candidate failing any gate is eliminated from primary standing regardless of its composite_score (which is retained for ranking/audit only). Gates are evaluated after scoring but override it.

hard_gates_are_dispositive.description: Always true — a failed hard gate eliminates a candidate irrespective of its composite_score.

gate_order.description: The order in which hard gates are evaluated (physical plausibility → timeline consistency → barrier logic).

primary_gate_status.description: Whether the card's primary hypothesis cleared all hard gates.

eliminated_candidates.description: Candidates removed from primary standing by a hard gate (or contradiction posture), sorted by descending composite_score so a high-scoring but gate-eliminated candidate is visible.

eliminating_gates.description: Gate(s)/posture(s) that eliminated this candidate (e.g. barrier_logic, timeline_consistency, documentary_contradiction).

note.description: Analyst-facing explanation of the elimination-first semantics.

causal_graph.description: N-6 unified, inspectable per-run causal graph. Consolidates the otherwise-scattered causal signals (TSKR chain_position, telemetry signal-DAG position, common-cause/explain-away links, near-tie competition, gate elimination) into ONE directed graph the analyst can see and contest, with committed edge directionality. Nodes are the target event and the assessed candidates; edges carry a relation type, a direction, and a basis. Deterministic and additive — it reflects existing scores, it does not change ranking.

target_event_id.description: Identifier of the abnormal event at the centre of the graph.

directionality_committed.description: True when at least one directed cause->effect edge could be committed from the available signals.

edges.description: Directed (or explicitly undirected) causal links between nodes, each with a basis and provenance.

relation.description: temporal_precedence = chain-position ordering vs the event; common_cause / explained_away = shared-cause links; near_tie = undirected competition between close-scoring hypotheses.

provenance_note.description: How the graph was assembled and the dual chain-position views (TSKR vs telemetry) it reconciles.
